claims.text: The target high-entropy alloys have varying compositions and microstructures.
The proposed feedback loop continuously adjusts computational models using experimental thermal-conductivity measurements.
The computational models predict thermal conductivity from alloy composition and microstructure.
Incorporating empirical thermal-behavior data through feedback will improve model accuracy.
The approach will improve predictive accuracy for identifying HEAs with low phonon thermal conductivity by at least 20% relative to traditional predictive methods.
Current predictive methods for HEA thermal conductivity rely primarily on theoretical models without real-time experimental feedback.
The approach is applicable to HEAs designed for thermal-insulation applications.
The approach may not extend to other material classes or applications.
The percentage improvement may vary with the materials and experimental conditions.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% accuracy improvement over traditional methods would falsify the hypothesis.
